question.problem: Let $T=[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & -8 & 0 \\ 6 & 10 & 0\end{aligned}]$ be the standard matrix of the linear transformation $T.$ Determine the value of $k$ for which the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 8 \\ k\end{aligned}]$ belongs to $\text{Im}(T).$
question.worked_solution:
The vector $v$ belongs to $\text{Im}(T)$ if there exists a vector $u=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]$  such that $T(u)=v.$

Therefore, we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot u & =v \\ [\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & -8 & 0 \\ 6 & 10 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 8 \\ k\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}4x-2y \\ 2x-8y \\ 6x+10y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 8 \\ k\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

This gives the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}4x-2y=2 \\ 2x-8y=8 \\ 6x+10y=k.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get $x=4+4y$, which we substitute into the first equation to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}4x-2y & =2 \\ 4(4+4y)-2y & =2 \\ 14y & =-14 \\ y & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, 

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =4+4y \\  & =4+4(-1) \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $x=0$ and $y=-1$ into the third equation and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}6x+10y & =k \\ 6(0)+10(-1) & =k \\ k & =-10.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $v\in \text{Im}(T)$ when $k=-10.$
